_comment: Data only. No code, no regular expressions. cleaner.js holds all logic; this file only names parameters. Keep every parameter name lowercase: the engine lowercases the name it reads from the URL before matching, so an entry with a capital letter silently never matches.
_neverStripComment: Absolute protection. These are never removed, whatever any other list says, and a future remotely-loaded rules file must not be able to override them. Three classes: destination parameters that hold the actual target address, access and security tokens, and core content identifiers.

hostRules.name: IMDb
hostRules._note: Amazon-family `ref_` records where you came from inside IMDb; the title/name id is in the path (/title/tt..., /name/nm...). Search filters (title_type, genres, sort, release_date, user_rating) and the `s` search scope are functional and deliberately left alone.

hostRules.name: Taobao / Tmall
hostRules._note: Product id lives in `id`, search text in `q`, variant in `skuid` - all protected by neverStrip. price, scene, activity_id, user_number_id and app are deliberately NOT stripped: ClearURLs removes them but two independent reviews flagged them as functional (price filter, promo screen routing, coupon id, shop id).

hostRules.name: Baidu Search
hostRules._note: Every name here was taken from a URL Baidu itself generated (submitting its own search box) and then verified live 2026-10-03: with the whole block present the result page is byte-for-byte the same page as without it. rsv_pq / rsv_t are a per-request id and a signed telemetry token; bs and oq are the PREVIOUS query, so they leak your search history into the next URL. tn and pn are deliberately NOT stripped: tn selects the vertical (tn=news renders Baidu's news tab instead of web results) and pn is the pagination offset (pn=10 is page two) - removing either fails invisibly, which is exactly the class of bug neverStrip exists for. ie is left alone too: Baidu autodetects the query encoding (a GBK wd read correctly with ie removed), so stripping it is risk without a privacy gain. rqlang (result language) and rn (results per page) are filters. The rest of the rsv_sug / rsv_idx family is deliberately NOT listed: those names turn up in other projects' lists but never appeared in a URL Baidu handed us and were never put through the live check, and an unverified name is exactly what this project refuses to copy. baidu.com covers every Baidu sub-product, so hosts where generic names like f or ch could be functional are excluded.

hostRules.name: Bilibili
hostRules._note: Keeps p (video part) and t (timestamp) - both verified live 2026-10-03: p=2 switches to part two, t=30 seeks. `mid` is the sharer id on content pages but the profile id on space.bilibili.com, so that host is excluded. `trackid` and `from_spmid` were found on bilibili's OWN links (home-page recommendations and /anime entries) and verified inert; trackid carries a per-session request id with a timestamp. `from` is left alone: verified inert on video pages, but it holds no identifier and spm_id_from already covers the same source info, so stripping a name that generic buys nothing. `callback` is rejected outright, not deferred: it is JSONP plumbing rather than an identifier, so removing it has no privacy upside. `theme` (movie layout on /bangumi) must stay.

hostRules.name: Xiaohongshu / RED
hostRules._note: xsec_token is an access token (neverStrip) - without it a note returns 404 or a login wall. xsec_source IS strippable: verified live 2026-10-03 on a real note, token kept and xsec_source removed - the note rendered in full (author, 62 CDN images) and Xiaohongshu re-appended xsec_source=pc_feed on its own, which is what settled the disagreement between reviews. On its own note links the site even emits xsec_source= empty. channel_type / parent_page_channel_type are navigation-source markers that the site itself drops from the URL on load. verify* are captcha state. type selects video vs gallery.

hostRules.name: Weibo
hostRules._note: api./service./passport. are excluded because display and retcode drive the OAuth dialog there. luicode and lfid carry the user's navigation chain between feeds.
